page0.text:
"...!"
I hear footsteps and stand up.
Someone's behind me. I can tell who's here without even needing to turn around.

page1.text:
The black-clad Servant is as stoic as ever.
Before, she wouldn't have announced herself with so much noise, so she must have done it for my benefit.

page2.text:
"What do you want, Rider?"
"..."
Rider looks down at me wordlessly.
...Hm.
Not that it matters, but Rider is tall. Something must be wrong with me to suddenly care about that.

page3.text:
"Is something funny, Shirou? I haven't said anything."
"Huh...? Oh, it's nothing. Rider, you're taller than me, right? I've seen you a few times, but I just noticed. I was laughing because I'm so oblivious."

page4.text:
"I see. You looked like you were struggling earlier, but it seems my concern was misplaced."
?
Is it just me, or does Rider sound a little angry?

page5.text: "Anyway, Rider, did you come help me today? I can't remember anything, but I feel like you carried me from the forest to the church."

page6.text: "...Yes. I carried you there. Sakura told me to protect you. I merely obeyed her order, as her Servant."

page7.text:
"Oh. I appreciate that, but that means she had to use her magical energy.
So..."
"Yes. Sakura has lost more of her already dwindling power. If Sakura continues to use me like she did today, I will devour her entirely."

page8.text:
Rider's voice is flat.
It doesn't contain any malice or pity for Sakura.
She's just stating the facts of being a Servant.

page9.text:
"Rider. Can I ask you something?"
"I do not mind. Ask your question."

page10.text:
"...Okay, then. Would you kill Sakura if she lost all of her Command Spells?"
A Master who runs out of Command Spells would typically get attacked by their own Servant.
If Sakura and Rider don't have a bond of trust, Rider will ruthlessly kill Sakura and use her body as fuel until she makes a pact with a new Master.

page11.text:
...Rider's only protecting Sakura as her Servant. It doesn't seem like it's out of any genuine affection.
That's why I need to determine her intentions here.

page12.text:
...
"So? Would you kill her?"
"Yes. If Sakura wishes it, I will put an end to her suffering myself. But Shirou, I want her to live."

page13.text:
"...Then, you won't attack her even if she doesn't have Command Spells?"
"The binding of the Command Spells has nothing to do with it. As long as Sakura is my Master, I will protect her of my own will. Because I am fond of her."

page14.text:
"Huh...really?"
"Yes. Does that surprise you that I have emotions of my own, Shirou?"
"Uh... No, sorry. I had the wrong idea. You don't seem that way, I just..."

page15.text:
"There is no need to apologize. I have never discussed it with Sakura, and she does not speak to me about it.
But, Shirou—a Master summons a Servant that is similar to them. It is no coincidence that you summoned Saber. Your souls must have been similar, somehow."

page16.text:
"Sakura and I are the same, in that sense.
Neither of us are talkative, so it stands to reason that conversations do not happen. But even without it, we understand each other."

page17.text:
...Rider's voice takes on a clearly warm tone.
From her appearance, I imagined her to be more cold and ruthless, but now I'm wondering if she's a truly gentle soul.

page18.text: "...Yeah. I'm glad to hear that. I'm very happy to know that Sakura has you on her side."

page19.text:
"You are? Then, it's my turn.
Shirou. Do you understand what Sakura has endured ever since she was adopted by the Makiris?"

page20.text:
"I..."
...I couldn't possibly understand.
Though, I've already heard from Kotomine's lips what happened to her.
"...I don't. That's why I don't think I should talk about it."

page21.text:
...Yeah.
I'm the lowest of mages, but even I know what kind of person Zouken is.
It's easy to imagine the awful things he's capable of, and it would probably be close to the truth.
Still...I could never claim to understand what Sakura's been through.

page22.text:
"Indeed. Sakura has been trying not to let you know. If you claimed that you understood it, then I would have killed you."
"...For Sakura's sake?"

page23.text:
"Yes. But it seems unnecessary now.
You are clumsy and inexperienced, but trustworthy at your core. That is how you have saved Sakura."

page24.text:
"...Before she met you, she was utterly resigned to her fate. For many years, every day was hopeless.
But she began to change when she met you. Shirou, you helped her to remember what it is like to feel emotions other than despair.
Pain and suffering were the greatest among them, but to someone who has only ever known despair, you were her one and only salvation."

page25.text:
"..."
I can't quite read the intent behind what Rider is saying.
I don't know why she came to love me, when she's suffered on a level that I could never possibly relate to.
But her words are utterly sincere, coming from someone who shares her senses with her Master.

page26.text:
Rider is quiet.
It's like she's speaking on Sakura's behalf.
"Shirou. You said that you would make Sakura happy, but to her,
these last two years have been the happiest times of her life."
Her voice contains quiet sadness and gratitude.

page27.text:
"That's all I wanted to ask you.
What makes Sakura happy is having you by her side. She does not wish for anything else."

page28.text:
Rider examines me through her blindfold.
...Her expression inquires if I understand the significance of what she's saying.
To Sakura Matou, Shirou Emiya fighting this war is a threat to her happiness.
Rider's challenging what I plan to do with this beat-up body of mine.

page29.text:
"But I..."
...I try to clench my unmoving left hand.
If I can still fight, then I have to, no matter what shape I'm in.

page30.text:
I swore that I'd save Sakura.
I decided that I'd fight for her sake now, not to end the war.
That's why...if I stop here, then I'll have nothing left.

page31.text:
"..."
Silence falls over us.
Rider stops talking, and I stare at the ground, not answering.
I wonder how much time passes.

page32.text:
"...Will you be on Sakura's side, Shirou?
No matter what happens from now on?"

page33.text:
...
The answer to her question is obvious.
Shirou Emiya swore to be Sakura Matou's ally.
I have to nod firmly.

page34.text:
...
I know that, but I can't say it out loud.
"No matter what happens?"
Deep inside myself, I realize what she means.

page35.text:
"...I understand. I won't press you, as the answer will be evident soon enough. I hope you are prepared for the consequences when that time comes."
Rider virtually blends into the darkness as she departs.
I watch her go, and then look up at the sky.

page36.text:
"...Damn it."
...Yeah.
She noticed that I couldn't give her a clear answer.

page37.text:
The black Shadow that I still don't understand.
This unstable left arm.
The ideals I've followed my entire life, that I decided to cast aside.
They all show me where I'm headed.
